data.narrative:
QunaSys is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $33M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 quantum computing peers—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Of the two valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector; while 6 same-sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints across narrow stage and valuation-tier filters. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $33M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $63M. This multiplier reflects typical step-up dynamics from Series B to subsequent rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M (low) to $72M (high), with a median of $63M. Given the single-method foundation, key uncertainties center on the applicability of the 1.9x stage multiplier to a frontier-tech vertical where fundraising dynamics and investor appetite may diverge materially from venture-stage norms. A fuller triangulation would require either sufficient same-stage peer data or alternative approaches such as comparable transaction analysis within quantum computing infrastructure. Until broader comparables emerge, the $53M–$72M range should be treated as provisional.
